title: Texture & Fabric Basket
strapline: Velvet, hessian, silk and sheepskin — a basket for scrunching, stroking, hiding under and finding out how soft feels.
intent: Offer sitting babies a whole vocabulary of touch — smooth silk, rough hessian, deep velvet, crinkly cellophane sewn safe inside a pocket.
Strengthen grasping, scrunching, pulling and releasing on materials that give, bunch and slide.
Support self-regulation and comfort — soft fabric soothes, and a muslin to pull over the face brings peekaboo within reach.
Grow early hiding-and-finding as treasures are wrapped, tucked into fabric bags and peeped under.
Keep a trusted adult close so the softest, most comforting exploring happens from a safe base.
implementation: Fill a basket with fabric variety: a velvet ribbon, a silk scarf, a square of hessian, a sheepskin offcut, a crocheted ball, a loofah mitt, a muslin, small drawstring bags with a treasure inside.
Sit the baby steadily with the basket in reach and settle low beside them, warm and unhurried.
Name the textures softly as the baby explores ('the velvet is so soft, the hessian is rough') and follow their lead.
Model a gentle peekaboo with the muslin and then let the baby take it over — hide your face, their face, a treasure.
Wash all fabrics between sessions, check drawstrings and stitching are secure, and keep any small hidden treasures larger than a choke tube.
key_questions: The silk is so smooth — and the hessian is scratchy. Can you feel both?
Where has your face gone under the muslin — peekaboo!
What's hiding inside the little bag?
Which soft thing helps you feel cosy?
Can you scrunch the scarf up small and let it spring open again?

impact.text: Babies explore the fabrics with hands and mouth, scrunching, stroking and pressing to find out how each one feels.
Babies grasp, pull and release the scarves and bags, working small hands on materials that give and bunch.
A soft square held to a cheek, a muslin pulled close — babies use the fabrics to soothe and settle themselves with an adult near.
A baby pulls the muslin over their face and off again, delighting in the disappear-and-return of peekaboo.
A baby tugs a treasure from a fabric bag, hides it back inside and finds it once more.

enhancements: A basket of muslins and scarves only, for a whole session of peekaboo and dancing fabric.
Sensory sewn squares — cellophane crinkle, ribbon loops, a jingle sewn safely inside a fabric pocket.
Drawstring bags with a wooden treasure hidden inside, so every bag is a small surprise.
A sheepskin laid out as the basket's base, warm and grounding under a settling baby.
A fabric tug-rope or knotted scarf strung low for pulling up and cruising along.

playing_exploring: The baby explores each fabric freely, following the pull of soft, rough, smooth and crinkly.
Touch leads the play — everything is scrunched, stroked, mouthed and pulled.
active_learning: Babies return to a comforting favourite and stay with the softest fabrics for long, calm stretches.
creating_thinking: Babies invent their own peekaboo and hiding games, wrapping and revealing on their own terms.
